raw_extract:
Canadian Experience Class

The Canadian Experience Class is for skilled workers who have Canadian work experience and want to become permanent residents.

Check your Canadian work experience

Your Canadian work experience must meet all the following requirements. It must

be in 1 or more of these NOC categories: training, education, experience and responsibilities (TEER) 0, 1, 2 or 3

Your experience can be in more than 1 job or NOC.

be gained by working in Canada (including the province of Quebec) while authorized to work under temporary resident status

If you worked remotely, you must have been physically in Canada and working for a Canadian employer.

show that you performed:

the actions in the lead statement of the NOC job description, and

most of the main duties listed

be paid work (you must have been paid wages or earned commission-volunteer work or unpaid internships don't count)

total at least 1 year of work or 1,560 hours total (30 hours per week) in the 3 years before you apply

Work experience you can't count

You can't count work experience if

you were studying full-time while you worked (co-op work terms also don't count)

you were self-employed (some physicians can count their time spent self-employed)

you were a volunteer or an unpaid intern

you were not legally allowed to work in Canada

How to count your work hours

You can meet the 1,560-hour requirement in a few different ways:

full-time at 1 job: up to 30 hours a week for 12 months = 1 year full-time (1,560 hours)

equal amount in part-time work: for example, 15 hours a week for 24 months = 1 year full time (1,560 hours)

full-time at more than 1 job: up to 30 hours a week combined across more than 1 job, for 12 months = 1 year full-time (1,560 hours)

Where you can live in Canada

When you fill out your profile, we'll ask you where you plan to live in Canada.

You must plan to live outside the province of Quebec. The province of Quebec selects its own skilled workers.
research_notes: Route recorded: the Canadian Experience Class (CEC), one of the three Express Entry programmes. Note that the URL requested (…/express-entry/eligibility/canadian-experience-class.html) redirected to …/express-entry/who-can-apply/canadian-experience-class.html and the page loaded under that final URL, which is the one recorded. CRITICAL POINT for a student corpus: the minimum qualifying period is 1 year (1,560 hours) of PAID skilled Canadian work experience gained while authorized to work as a temporary resident - which for a graduate is typically the PGWP period - and it must fall within the 3 years before the application. A student's full-time study work does NOT count: 'You can't count work experience if you were studying full-time while you worked (co-op work terms also don't count)'. So co-op placements cannot be run back-to-back to manufacture PR eligibility; the student must be out of full-time study and working. Also excluded: self-employment (bar a narrow physician policy), volunteering, unpaid internships, and work done without authorization. Quebec is excluded from CEC entirely. Not verified here and therefore not claimed: the Express Entry points grid, CRS cut-off scores (which are invitation-dependent and change per draw), the Federal Skilled Worker Program's 1-year requirement, and Provincial Nominee Program streams - the PNP is usually the faster PR route for international graduates and a corpus entry that names only CEC would be misleading, but I did not fetch a PNP source so no PNP figure is asserted here.

claims.statement: The Canadian Experience Class requires at least 1 year of work, or 1,560 hours total (30 hours per week), of skilled Canadian work experience in the 3 years before applying.
Qualifying work must be paid, must be in a NOC TEER 0, 1, 2 or 3 category, and must have been performed in Canada while authorized to work under temporary resident status.
Work done while studying full-time does not count toward CEC, and co-op work terms also do not count.
The CEC is not available to applicants who plan to live in Quebec, which selects its own skilled workers.
